A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, algorithms, and theoretical development. Their complete main texts, table, equations, and Appendices A-D support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v4 presents algorithms, theoretical guarantees, and proofs, including its appendices. Empirical examples are attributed to other work; no original experimental or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v5 remains a theoretical paper throughout the main text and appendices. Its empirical RLHF examples concern cited research, and it reports no original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same least-squares estimation, exploration bonuses, Gibbs-policy updates, and backward value-iteration procedures.

E1.justification: Neither version evaluates datasets or empirical tasks. The newly discussed linear and tabular MDP results belong to cited research, not additional evaluations by this work.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Online Iterative GSHF, Two-Stage Mixed-Policy Sampling, Online Iterative M-GSHF, and XPO as theoretical comparators. The added Tiapkin citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version documents an empirical evaluation protocol, and no experiments, metrics, splits, or training budgets are introduced.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or case analyses. Appendices A-D contain theoretical proofs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated experiments, seeds, error bars, or empirical significance tests. The retained high-probability guarantees are theoretical statements.

E6.justification: Table 1 retains the same regret and sample-complexity entries, and the work's reported guarantees remain unchanged. No original empirical result entries or findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, Theorems 4.1 and 5.1, and Appendix A-D proof arguments retain their substance. The new Zhao et al. citation accompanies an already-present moment inequality; equation renumbering and auxiliary-expression labeling do not revise the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims of logarithmic online regret without additional coverage assumptions and novel bandit and MDP decompositions.

C2.justification: The optimism-based mechanism explanations, absolute-reward scope, and acknowledged additional horizon dependence remain unchanged. The added Impact Statement provides no substantive new limitation or interpretation.

D1.justification: Algorithm pseudocode, confidence-set and bonus specifications, and planning-oracle descriptions are retained. No implementation resources, hardware information, or code/data access instructions are added.

R1.justification: v5 adds Tiapkin et al. (2023, 2024), distinguishing their fast-rate pure-exploration results from online regret minimization. Appendix A also newly attributes its existing moment inequality to Lemma 2.14 of Zhao et al. (2025).

P1.justification: v5 adds an introductory paragraph and generic Impact Statement, revises front matter and acknowledgements, and changes equation numbering. The section sequence and most explanatory prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes an ICML document with two-column main text and references, new running headers, and extensive equation and algorithm reflow. Table 1 moves to a page-top display spanning both columns, while the retained appendices are also retypeset.

improvement.justification: The added pure-exploration comparison in Section 1 clarifies the research gap, and Appendix A gains explicit sourcing for an existing inequality. These provide a modest scholarly improvement without changing the scientific results. Removing v4's named acknowledgement of help correcting a proof is a countervailing loss of attribution.
